about.what: LLM Light profiles. A profile is one named bundle of classifier, routing, cache, budget, audit and Claude Code settings. lib/llmlight.mjs renders it into a LiteLLM config, the routing hook (assets/llmlight_router.py) and Claude Code settings, for a laptop (Anthropic API) or a sandbox (Bedrock).
about.tiers: Rules route to a tier, never to a model name. The target maps tiers to models: local = claude-opus-5 / claude-sonnet-5 / claude-haiku-4-5 on the Anthropic API; sandbox = optimize.mjs MODELS (opus45 / sonnet46; small falls back to sonnet46 until a Haiku id is enabled on Bedrock).
about.classifier: source 'rules' decides per request from the call kind alone. 'session-classes' also bakes the project's classes from Hub → Triage (Jev's answers) into the profile when it is applied, so a request never waits on a classifier call. unclear: what the main loop does when Jev said unclear.
about.rule-vocabulary: when: {call: main|subagent|background, capability|urgency|latency|deferral|context: <class or [classes]>, minMessages: n, maxTools: n}; to: frontier|mid|small. First match wins; neverDowngrade keywords in the request pin it to frontier.
about.audit: log: off | decisions | full. Lines hold numbers and names only, never prompt or response text. judgeSampleRate is the share of routed turns queued for a blind re-grade.

profiles.title: Laptop · guarded
profiles.for: interactive development — a person is waiting on every reply
profiles.summary: The coding loop stays on the frontier model. Only the calls nobody reads closely move: Claude Code's background calls (titles, summaries) go small, subagents go mid. The safest place to start.

profiles.title: Laptop · follows Triage
profiles.for: interactive development on projects Triage has already classified
profiles.summary: Like guarded, but the main loop follows the project's classes: where Jev said the work needs a mid model, the main loop runs mid. Where Jev said unclear, it stays on the frontier until a sandbox re-run answers.

rules.why: Triage: project work fits a small model
Triage: project work fits a mid model

profiles.title: Sandbox · lean
profiles.for: unattended agents — nobody is waiting, so latency is free
profiles.summary: Everything starts on the mid model and falls back to the frontier on error. Thinking and turns are capped, the run has a hard spend ceiling at the proxy, and one routed turn in ten is queued for a blind re-grade.

rules.why: Triage: project needs the frontier model

profiles.title: CI · strict
profiles.summary: Mid model throughout with no escalation, a $2 hard ceiling per run and 30 turns. A job that needs more fails loudly instead of spending quietly.

profiles.title: Frontier · governed
profiles.for: security reviews, compliance work, anything that must not be downgraded
profiles.summary: No routing at all: every call runs on the frontier model. The profile adds only a daily budget and a full audit trail, so the cost of doing it the expensive way is visible.
